- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.5), model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next period.
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.5), model often underestimates; increase forecast by 2–5% to align with mean-reversion bias.
- Model consistently overreacts to recent spikes (e.g., 80+ → 85+), leading to overshoot; cap forecast at +10% above recent peak unless sentiment supports continuation.
- After a sharp drop (e.g., 85→70), model fails to fully correct; add 1–3% downward bias to compensate for lagged mean reversion.
- If sentiment is neutral (0.0) and history shows volatility, model overfits short-term noise; apply smoothing filter (e.g., 3-period moving average) to reduce false peaks.
- Forecast horizon 30d often misses 1–2 week mean-reversion window; adjust by adding 1–2% downward bias after 14-day mark if sentiment remains flat.
